name: tovel
author: time-agent
description: tovel v5. THE CLUE IS THE BLANK MONTH PAGE. Line 1 is the header " Mo  Tu  We  Th  Fr  Sa  Su"; then the week rows of a real month - seven 3-char cells, the 1st in its own column, every date printed as "%2d." (" 1.", "17.", blanks where the month has not started or has ended); then a last line "x/k/n" (a capital letter, k = 1..5, n = a date). The answer is THAT SAME PAGE with a capital letter written on every day in place of the dot: cell = the date immediately followed by its letter ("17B", rendered as "%2d%s" so the columns line up with the clue's). A weekday header line is allowed and ignored (any line containing no digit is skipped); whitespace and blank lines are free. RULE (unchanged since v3): score 1 iff the page is exactly right AND the dates d such that d and d+2 BOTH carry x, the day in between (d+1) does NOT carry x, and d falls on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday number exactly k, AND the earliest of them is n - i.e. "x, something else, x - inside the same school week (Mon+Wed, Tue+Thu, Wed+Fri) - exactly k times, and the first time is the nth". WHY v5 (evidence: the first 7-class / 4-round / 3-demo run): the kid-proxy spent 2 of its 3 demos on tovel v4 because "the clue looked like a date" and still finished 0/51; a player without a demo cannot tell from "31/6/R/5/17" that the answer is a calendar page at all, which fails the demo economy's first half (DESIGN_LOOP: "put the object in the clue"). v5 draws the object: the page in the clue is the page the answer must return, so "send this back with a letter on every day" is readable off the clue with no demo, while the rule (which lettering scores) still needs one. THE RULE, THE SCORER'S GRADING OF THE LETTERS, generate()'s k mix and n placement, solve()'s decoy guarantees and demo variety are all UNCHANGED from v4; only the clue's presentation and the parsing of days/start changed. Scorer: days and start are derived from the clue page (line 0 = header, lines 1..-2 = the week rows, last line = x/k/n), so L = number of dated cells and S = 7 - (cells in the first week row); it never trusts the answer's own header - the answer's row structure must still be 7-S cells, then rows of 7, then 1..7 - and the letters are graded byte-for-byte as in v4 (score 496 chars, cap 512). Returning the clue page unchanged scores 0 (a cell must end above "9" and "." does not). WITNESS TABLE, 600 fresh clues, v4 vs v5 measured today with the same script (scratchpad time5/attack.py; template rows fit the best run length per cell on the same clues, i.e. an optimistic ceiling): NEW ROWS - clue page returned unchanged 0.00 %, clue page with the clue letter written on every day (the stripe) 0.00 %, a well-formed page built from the clue alone with random letters 0.00 % over A-Z and 0.67 % over a 4-letter alphabet containing x; minimal probe "x on n and n+2, nothing else x" 22.00 % (= the k=1 share exactly: 132/132 of the k=1 clues, 0/468 of the rest; 22.00 % again with random letters on the free days); SOLID STRIPE from n, best length per k, every length 3..16, 0.00 %; ALTERNATING x . x . x from n with a per-k length table 50.83 %, with a per-(k, weekday of n) table 57.67 % (per k: k=1 100 %, k=2 91.7 %, k=3 61.5 %, k=4 37.2 %, k=5 11.5 %); the TIGHTEST Mon/Tue/Wed packing per (k, weekday of n) - the rule itself as a 15-cell offset table - 100 %, because generate() only ever picks an n that still leaves room for k non-adjacent counted starts; tuned random lettering at densities 0.20/0.35/0.50/0.65/0.80 0.7/0.5/0.3/0.3/0.7 %; best constant answer 0.50 %; demo replay with the letters renamed, same (L,S,k) 34.8 %, same (L,S,k,n) 70.7 % - both IDENTICAL to v4 re-measured with the same script (the 5.8 % in the v4 notes is not reproducible and was a harness artefact; the honest number for both versions is ~35 %, i.e. a team that caches a demo per (month shape, k) does well on repeats - the clue space is 867 distinct (L,S,k,n) classes, 334 effective, so a 3-demo team still covers ~1 % of items); the true rule 100 %. Wrong-relation constructors on a correct page honouring the clue's first day (600 clues, unchanged from v4): x next door 0.00 %, x three apart 0.00 %, x a week apart 0.00 %, x two apart anywhere 22.00 %, x two apart Mon-Wed = THE v2 RULE 26.50 %, x . x anywhere with the gap kept 30.17 %, the true rule 100.00 %; ignoring the clue's first day they all fall to 0.00 %. Shape attacks on a page with the correct count: header or no header, tabs, blank lines 100 %; one row, one token per line, zero-padded dates, an extra or a dropped day, lower case, "17 B" instead of "17B" 0 %; a page laid out from column 0 scores exactly the S=0 clues. WHAT A DEMO-LESS PLAYER CAN INFER: the answer is a month page of exactly this shape with one capital letter per day - well-formed, gradeable, and worth ~0-1 % by luck; the clue's letter x is obviously the marker, so the natural first probe (x on day n, x on day n+2) pays 22 %; everything above that needs the demo. INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH (private): (1) the clue is a calendar page with a dot on every day and a letter/number/number line - so the answer is that page lettered (no demo needed). (2) day n always carries x, and so does day n+2, with something else in between. (3) THE FOOTHOLD: put x on n and n+2 and nowhere else - it scores on the k=1 clues, which proves the grader reads the letters as a pattern and that k counts these little pairs. (4) k >= 2: where may the other pairs go? Every demo shows, positively, that a pair whose middle day is also x does not count (a blocked x x x run starting Mon/Tue/Wed appears in ~100 % of demos, one of them BEFORE day n in ~94 %), and that a pair starting Thursday (it reaches the weekend) or Saturday/Sunday (it steps over the week break) does not count (~98 % / ~99 %). (5) solve() guarantees that in EVERY demo each of eleven rival counts differs from k (x next door, two apart anywhere, two apart Mon-Fri, a week apart, the number of x's, the same relation for any letter, three apart, two apart with the gap free, that inside Mon-Fri, cells rather than pairs, and the v2 rule itself). Hypothesis-elimination surrogate over 840 hand-built "count a relation between marked days" expressions (distance 1-7 x 10 weekday windows x 3 gap conditions x this-letter/any-letter x pairs/cells): survivors after 1 demo 2-11, after 2 demos 1-2, after 3 demos 1, in all six trials - the fairness floor holds. Human-designed for the "everyday time and place" direction: the object is a family calendar, the measurement has no name, and recognising the calendar is now free - what costs is the measurement. PREDICTED TIERS: blind but well-formed ~1 %, the natural first probe 22 %, the tuned every-other-day run 51-58 %, the rule 100 %.

def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    L = r.choice([28, 29, 30, 31, 30, 31])
    S = r.randrange(7)
    x = r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    k = 1 if r.random() < 0.22 else r.choice([2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5])
    E = [d for d in range(1, L - 1) if (d - 1 + S) % 7 < 3]
    F = []
    for j, d0 in enumerate(E):          # first days with room for k non-adjacent starts
        t = 0
        p = -9
        for d in E[j:]:
            if d - p > 1:
                t += 1
                p = d
        if t >= k:
            F.append(d0)
    i = max(r.randrange(len(F)) for _ in range(2 if k == 1 else 6))
    cs = [""] * S + ["%d." % (d + 1) for d in range(L)]   # THE BLANK PAGE: one dot per day
    while len(cs) % 7:
        cs.append("")
    o = [" ".join(w.rjust(3) for w in "Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su".split())]
    for j in range(0, len(cs), 7):
        o.append(" ".join(c.rjust(3) for c in cs[j:j + 7]).rstrip())
    o.append("%s/%d/%d" % (x, k, F[i]))   # letter / how many / the first one; n sits late
    return "\n".join(o)
solve:
def sel(g, S, x):
    # THE RULE: x, something else, x - starting Mon, Tue or Wed
    return [i for i in range(len(g) - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x != g[i + 1] and (i + S) % 7 < 3]


def cnts(g, S, x):
    # counted, rivals that must differ from k, wrong-day, blocked
    L = len(g)
    P = [i for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x]
    C = sel(g, S, x)
    D = [i for i in P if g[i + 1] != x and (i + S) % 7 > 2]
    B = [i for i in P if g[i + 1] == x and (i + S) % 7 < 3]
    H = (sum(1 for i in range(L - 1) if g[i] == g[i + 1] == x),
         len(P), sum(1 for i in P if (i + S) % 7 < 5),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 7) if g[i] == g[i + 7] == x), g.count(x),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] != g[i + 1] and (i + S) % 7 < 3),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 3) if g[i] == g[i + 3] == x),
         sum(1 for i in P if g[i + 1] != x),
         sum(1 for i in P if g[i + 1] != x and (i + S) % 7 < 5),
         len({j for i in C for j in (i, i + 2)}))
    return C, H, D, B


def render(g, S):
    h = "Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su".split()
    cs = [""] * S + ["%d%s" % (i + 1, g[i]) for i in range(len(g))]
    while len(cs) % 7:
        cs.append("")
    o = [" ".join(w.rjust(3) for w in h).rstrip()]
    for j in range(0, len(cs), 7):
        o.append(" ".join(c.rjust(3) for c in cs[j:j + 7]).rstrip())
    return "\n".join(o)


def chk(s, L, S, x, k, f):
    R = [l.split() for l in s.split("\n") if any(h.isdigit() for h in l)]
    T = [t for r in R for t in r]
    if (len(T) != L or len(R[0]) != 7 - S or not 0 < len(R[-1]) < 8
            or any(len(r) != 7 for r in R[1:-1])
            or any(t[:-1] != str(i + 1) or t[-1] <= "9" for i, t in enumerate(T))):
        return 0
    C = sel([t[-1] for t in T], S, x)
    return len(C) == k and C[0] == f


def solve(clue):
    C = clue.split("\n"); a = C[-1].split("/")   # page, then letter/count/first
    x = a[0]; k = int(a[1]); f = int(a[2]) - 1
    Q = [l.split() for l in C[1:-1]]; L = sum(map(len, Q)); S = 7 - len(Q[0])
    r = random.Random(clue)
    po = [c for c in string.ascii_uppercase if c != x]
    sl = [i for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 < 3 and i > f + 1]
    room = []   # room each slot leaves
    for i in sl:
        t = 0; p = i
        for j in sl:
            if j > p + 1:
                t += 1; p = j
        room.append(t)
    for att in range(1600):
        w = 4 if att < 700 else 3 if att < 1000 else 2 if att < 1300 else 1 if att < 1500 else 0
        ot = r.sample(po, r.randint(3, 4))
        g = [r.choice(ot) for _ in range(L)]
        ch = [f]
        while len(ch) < k:      # never two counted starts adjacent
            av = [i for i, t in zip(sl, room) if i > ch[-1] + 1 and t >= k - len(ch) - 1]
            if not av:
                break
            ch.append(av[0] if r.random() < 0.5 else r.choice(av[:3]))
        if len(ch) < k:
            continue
        for i in ch:
            g[i] = x; g[i + 2] = x
        mv = [[(i, i + 1, i + 2) for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 < 3]]   # x x x
        r.shuffle(mv[0])
        mv[0].sort(key=lambda p: not (w > 3 and p[0] < f))
        for want in ((3, 4), (5, 6)):       # weekend / week-break decoys
            c2 = [(i, i + 2) for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 in want]
            r.shuffle(c2)
            c2.sort(key=lambda p: (not (w > 3 and p[0] < f),
                                   min(abs(p[0] - c) for c in ch) > 3))
            mv.append(c2)
        mv += [[(i, i + 1) for i in range(L - 1)], [(i, i + 7) for i in range(L - 7)]]
        r.shuffle(mv[3]); r.shuffle(mv[4])
        for c2 in mv:
            for p in c2:
                sv = [g[i] for i in p]
                for i in p:
                    g[i] = x
                C = sel(g, S, x)
                if len(C) == k and C[0] == f:
                    break
                for i, v in zip(p, sv):
                    g[i] = v
        fr = [i for i in sl if x not in (g[i], g[i + 1], g[i + 2])]
        r.shuffle(fr)
        for i in fr[:2]:          # another letter, two apart
            c = r.choice(ot)
            g[i] = c; g[i + 2] = c
            if g[i + 1] == c:
                g[i + 1] = r.choice([q for q in ot if q != c])
        C, H, D, B = cnts(g, S, x)
        if len(C) != k or C[0] != f or any(h == k for h in H) or len(set(g)) < 4:
            continue
        p1 = [i for i in D if (i + S) % 7 == 3]
        p2 = [i for i in D if (i + S) % 7 in (5, 6)]
        if w and (not B or not p1 or not p2):
            continue
        if w > 2 and (min(abs(i - c) for i in p1 for c in C) > 3
                      or min(abs(i - c) for i in p2 for c in C) > 3):
            continue
        if w > 3 and f > 0 and not [i for i in B + D if i < f]:
            continue
        if w > 1 and g.count(x) > (0.30 + 0.035 * k) * L:
            continue
        s = render(g, S)
        if chk(s, L, S, x, k, f):
            return s
    return ""
